5. The learned Advocate-on-record for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that the prosecution witnesses made departure from the prosecution case and further the High Court Division has not said a single word as how the petitioners are liable for the offence for which they were convicted and the present case is virtually is also a case of no evidence as because not a single prosecution witness has stated anything as to the involvement of petitioners in connection with the offence charged; the High Court Division, without at all considering the case of the petitioners that they did not issue any token on that particular time and date, arrived at an erroneous conclusion that the petitioners knowing fully well about the forged bills issued tokens specially when the prosecution did not take any steps to seize the register of tokens and make the same as exhibit; in the absence of strict proof of the fact that the petitioners issued the tokens knowing fully well about the forgery of bills and advices, the convictions can not be sustained inasmuch as per Banking Department Manual token clerk would receive the bills and issue token taking signature of the party but in the present case there is no such evidence to the effect that the petitioners receiving the bills issued tokens after taking signature of the party but inspite of the above, the petitioners were convicted without fixing their specific liability which has caused a total failure of justice. 

 7. Regarding the question as to whether in the instant case the G.D. Entry, being the first information of a cognizable offence to the police was the FIR, the High Court Division found substance in the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney General that Anti Corruption Department after taking up the matter proceeded as per the Anti Corruption Rules and after making preliminary enquiry lodged an F.I.R. and then took up the investigation and that anti corruption cases are treated as special cases and those are governed by the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (Act No. XL of 1958) and the Anti Corruption Rules which have been framed under section 12 of the Act 1958. 

 10. It thus appears that the High Court Division dismissed the appeal having found that the petitioners and others formed a gang to misappropriate the money from the Government Exchequer of which they are the custodians and on elaborately discuss of the evidence, they were found guilty under sections 409/109 and also 471/109 and 472/109 of the Penal Code and the charge against the petitioners having been proved beyond all reasonable doubt there was no illegality in the impugned judgment and order of conviction so as to call for any interference.
